newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK GOVERNMENT BACKS OFF ON JOURNALIST BAN.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK GOVERNMENT BACKS OFF ON JOURNALIST BAN.

text.p: The Slovak government backed away on Friday from a decision to bar four reporters apparently caught up in a feud between the country's president and prime minister from government briefings.

The four were among a group of journalists who publicly denied allegations made by Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar that President Michal Kovac had told them at a news briefing in May that Meciar was suffering from a brain tumour.

Meciar spokeswoman Magda Pospisilova announced the decision after a meeting between the government press department and representatives of Slovakia's two journalist unions, newspaper publishers and the Association of European Journalists.

"As a result of today's meeting at which all the participants agreed on the need to calm the situation, the government press department has decided to rescind its previous decision," said a joint statement read by Pospisilova.

Tuesday's decision spurred a wave of protests among journalists and publishers and the biggest journalist union, the Slovak Syndicate of Journalists, appealed to the International Federation of Journalists for support.
The government said it had barred the four from regular government news conferences for "personal reasons".
Kovac and Meciar, once allies, have been locked in a bitter political battle since Kovac called on parliament to hold a vote of confidence in Meciar in 1994.
The government has come under scrutiny in the past two years for alleged foot-dragging over democratic reforms.
The European Union and United States have expressed concerns over the development of democracy in Slovakia.
